claim:full-corpus-reproduction.proposition: Running the full BioModels corpus through the batch-compare-biomodels composite under up to five independent ODE engines reproduces 1008 models (14.7M timecourse rows) at corpus scale: 306 models are covered by all five engines and 725 by four or more. This study establishes COVERAGE — how broadly each model is cross-run and that the per-model, per-engine trajectories are committed and browsable model-by-model in the corpus explorer. Scored trajectory AGREEMENT against the BioSimulators reference is measured in the sibling repeat-matching study (currently on the BIOMD1-3 validation subset), not quantified corpus-wide here.
claim:full-corpus-reproduction.hypothesis: Standards-based SBML/SED-ML models integrate to the same solution regardless of engine; systematic disagreement flags a model-encoding ambiguity or an engine-specific numerical behaviour.

claim:repeat-matching.proposition: On the BIOMD1-3 validation subset, the live engines reproduce the BioSimulators SED-ML reference arm exactly wherever an observable is computed: after iteration 2 ("full observable coverage"), all 12 repeat arms (copasi/tellurium/amici/pysces × the models they cover) match the reference under numpy allclose with zero numerical mismatches; the only residual is coverage (2 reference observables in BIOMD3 are not yet computed by any engine). Cross-engine reproducibility is likewise exact where observables overlap (22/30 pairs exact; the 8 residuals are pysces computing 2/65 observables differently and simbio exposing a reduced 48-observable set). The dominant failure mode is observable coverage, not numerical divergence — confirming the study hypothesis.
claim:repeat-matching.hypothesis: Where an observable is computed at all, the current study reproduces the previous study exactly; the dominant failure mode is coverage (missing SED-ML dataGenerator observables) rather than numerical divergence. Each recovered reproducibility match — especially bringing simbio, the new engine, onto the engines that already agree — is worth 10x a broken repeat match.

provenance.note: All 12 iter2 repeat arms have matched == total (numpy allclose at the reference study's tolerances). Derived from the committed parquet.

narrative.question: Across the full BioModels corpus, do independent ODE simulators (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) reproduce the same trajectories for the same model — and where do they diverge?
